title: Open Values Door v0.1
description: The file a site publishes at /.well-known/open-values.json to say what it offers: which version of the standard it follows, its privacy promises, its licences, and every facts file it publishes with a hash to check it against. The site's build writes it.

format.description: Always "open-values-door". Tells a reader that this file is a site's public list of what it publishes.

version.description: The version of the door format this file follows, 0.1.

generatedAt.description: When the site build wrote this file, as an ISO 8601 date and time in UTC, such as "2026-10-13T09:00:00Z".

self.description: The address this file is served at, normally the site's /.well-known/open-values.json.

publisher.description: Who publishes the site: a name and a web address.

version.description: The version of the standard the site follows, such as "0.1".

url.description: The address of the page that explains the standard.

spec.description: The address of the written specification.

standard.description: Which version of the Open Values Standard the site follows, and where to read it.

name.description: The app's name, such as "Conscious Consuming".

role.description: What the app is for among apps that use the standard, such as "reference-instance" for the one the standard is checked against.

index.description: The address of the app's list of facts files (its data index).

cards.description: The address of the app's shareable result cards.

instance.description: The app on this site that uses the standard: its name, its role and where its data lives.

licenses.description: The licences that cover the site, as web addresses keyed by what they cover, such as code, data, and guides and docs.

accounts.description: Whether the site has user accounts.

payToRank.description: Whether anyone can pay to change a ranking.

passportLocation.description: Where a person's values file is kept, such as "local-device" for their own browser.

privacy.description: What the site does and does not do with the people who use it. Each answer is true or false.

trustArtifacts.description: Addresses of public records a reader can check, keyed by name, such as the funding ledger and the citation bundles.

index.description: The address of the list of fixed copies (a stack index file).

pattern.description: The address pattern for one fixed copy. Replace {id} with the facts file's id and {sha256} with its hash.

hash.description: Always "sha256": the hash used to name and check the copies.

stacks.description: Where to find fixed copies of each facts file, named by their SHA-256 hash, so a copy can be checked after download.

agents.description: Optional. How an AI agent should read this commons: a plain-language summary, and a read-only Model Context Protocol server.

llms.description: The address of a plain-text summary of the site written for AI systems (llms.txt).

transport.description: How to connect to the server, such as "streamable-http".

tools.description: The names of the tools the server offers, such as "search" and "fetch".

readOnly.description: True when the server can only read data and cannot change anything.

logsQueries.description: Whether the server keeps a log of the questions sent to it.

mcp.description: A Model Context Protocol server an AI agent can use to search and read the data.

lenses.description: Every facts file the site publishes, with where to get it and the hash to check it against.

id.description: The facts file's id, such as "banking".

title.description: The facts file's name as shown to people.

type.description: What kind of thing its entries are: Products, Services, Media, Organizations or Initiatives.

domain.description: The area of life it belongs to in the site's navigation, such as "Money".

group.description: The group it sits in inside that area, where it has one.

entries.description: How many entries the file holds.

criteria.description: The keys of the criteria its entries are scored on.

url.description: The address of the page in the app that shows this file's rankings.

data.description: The address of the file's JSON data.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 hash of the data file's bytes, 64 hexadecimal characters.

integrity.description: The same hash written as "sha256-" followed by the hex digest.

stack.description: The address of the fixed copy of this exact version of the file.

license.description: The address of the licence the data is published under.

source.description: Where the facts come from as a whole, copied from the file's meta.

attribution.description: The file's attribution paragraph, copied from its meta: what it covers and which sources it uses.

asof.description: The most recent year among the dates on the file's sourced claims.

sourceAsOf.description: The oldest and newest years among the dates on the file's sourced claims.
